term: realism, radical skepticism and God in #122
definition: Realism, radical skepticism and God existence are the source’s unelaborated propositions. The argument separately assumes realism-without-God implies radical skepticism, rejects radical skepticism, and asserts realism before its God conclusion.
note: No particular realism domain, global knowledge logic, divine explanatory role or classical God signature is selected. Epistemic failure and ontic falsity differ; the realism/skepticism bridge and truth of realism remain open. A propositional transcription would not independently defend them.
